sections.title: The Universality of Sin
observations: In this section, Paul emphasizes that all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God. He argues that both Jews and Gentiles are under sin, highlighting the universal need for salvation.
Paul uses the Old Testament to support his claim, quoting various scriptures that depict the sinful nature of humanity. This underscores the idea that no one is righteous on their own.

sections.title: Justification by Faith
observations: Paul introduces the concept of justification by faith apart from the works of the law. He explains that righteousness comes through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe.
This section is crucial as it shifts the focus from the law to faith, emphasizing that salvation is a gift from God and not something that can be earned.

sections.title: The Role of the Law
observations: Paul discusses the purpose of the law, stating that it reveals sin but cannot save. The law serves to show humanity their need for a Savior.
He clarifies that faith does not nullify the law; rather, it upholds it by fulfilling its ultimate purpose.

importantVerses.commentary: For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God. This verse encapsulates the human condition and the need for redemption.
For we hold that one is justified by faith apart from works of the law. This verse is central to the doctrine of justification by faith.
Do we then overthrow the law by this faith? By no means! On the contrary, we uphold the law. This verse clarifies the relationship between faith and the law.

questions: What does it mean to be justified by faith, and how does this differ from justification by works?
How does the universality of sin affect our understanding of God's grace?
In what ways does the law serve a purpose in the life of a believer today?
